source_findings.finding: The fresh solver interpreter and top-level trusted worker imports run before worker.py:46 lowers RLIMIT_CPU to 8/9 for a short request; seccomp setup then precedes runpy. The parent records total direct-child wait4 user+system CPU, not a runpy-only interval. Trusted child initialization, user imports, native calls and final state serialization are consequently inside that measured total.

The protected supervisor and outer bwrap CPU are not added to the authoritative direct-child measurement. Blocking wait4 and a separate parent SIGALRM timer remain in use; this is not the historical trusted-parent polling-CPU path.

Before its own lowering call, the child should inherit the outer short-run CPU guard of 10/11. Thus merely observing that some startup precedes the 8/9 setter does not itself account for 17.117624 CPU seconds. The actual inherited limits, phase CPU values and kill cause were not recorded in the provided observation.

The v3 solver starts its CPU origin at zero and reserves 0.60 CPU seconds, consistent with typical reported short totals near 5.4. It does not reset the origin after scientific-library imports. Its native loop checks deadlines between operations and the final np.savez/write_bytes path has no Clock check. These are plausible mechanisms for a smaller cooperative-budget overrun, not an established explanation for defeating a kernel hard9 guard.

The inspected native loader loads the completed local_solver.so in-process. A bounded search of the five inspected production text files found no resource-limit, signal-mask or process-creation changes. No binary-to-source equivalence or native binary behavior was attested, and the shared object was not loaded by this review.

An outer exit value of 137 alone does not identify which kill path occurred. The protected worker_exitcode and worker_timed_out distinguish the reported child termination from the supervisor wall-time action; separate wait4 user/system components and pre-user phase measurements are missing from the provided totals.
